clusters.label: Payoff Table Structure
clusters.rationale: These candidates all describe the payoff table as a fundamental structure in decision making, with rows for alternatives, columns for states of nature, and payoffs in cells. They represent the same teachable concept of understanding and constructing payoff tables regardless of the specific example context.

clusters.label: Maximax (Optimistic) Decision Criterion
clusters.rationale: These candidates describe the same optimistic decision rule: choosing the alternative with the maximum of the maximum payoffs. The approach is identical, just applied to different example contexts (profit vs. cost). The underlying concept of selecting the best of the best outcomes is the same.

clusters.label: Maximin (Conservative/Pessimistic) Decision Criterion
clusters.rationale: These candidates describe the same conservative decision rule: choosing the alternative with the maximum of the minimum payoffs. The concept is identical across the profit and cost examples, focusing on guaranteeing the best worst-case outcome.

clusters.label: Minimax Regret Decision Criterion
clusters.rationale: These candidates all describe the minimax regret criterion, which involves constructing a regret table and selecting the alternative with the smallest maximum regret. The core procedure is the same, regardless of whether payoffs are profits or costs.

clusters.label: Decision Making Under Uncertainty
clusters.rationale: These candidates introduce the broader context of decision making without probabilities, emphasizing uncertainty. c18_pro_thinking_001 defines uncertainty, while c16_pro_thinking_001 frames the cost-based example. Both are about understanding the environment where decision criteria are applied without known probabilities.

clusters.label: Laplace Criterion
clusters.rationale: This candidate uniquely describes the Laplace criterion, which assumes equal probabilities for states of nature and selects the alternative with the highest average payoff. It is distinct from the other decision criteria because it uses averaging, not maximax or minimax.

clusters.label: Hurwicz Criterion
clusters.rationale: This candidate uniquely describes the Hurwicz criterion, which uses a coefficient of optimism to balance best and worst payoffs. It is a distinct decision rule not covered by the others.

clusters.label: Advanced Regret Theory Concepts
clusters.rationale: These candidates from c17_pro_thinking cover advanced aspects of minimax regret, including formal regret definition, Bernoulli equivalent rules, worst case prior, and memory rules for bandit problems. They are related to a deeper theoretical treatment of minimax regret but are not the same as the basic application of the criterion. Grouping them together because they all extend the core regret concept to bandit problems and theoretical proofs, which is likely beyond the scope of a basic lesson on decision-making tools. They may be pruned later if not central.
